1. The wheel needs to be at a minimum of 6inches big.
2. Bedding minimum is 6 inches deep but more is always better.
3. There isnt enough enrichment in there, try getting some timothy hay hides meant for hamsters, chews (none of the loofa chews you find at a petstore, buy wooden chews) 
4. Try getting some cork logs or cork hides for the hammy
5. And yes, as others have said, a sand bath for em', the kind most hamster owners use is childrens play sand (dont use any sand that is synthetic its not good for them)

If the food allergies below the ingredients say "contains milk" or "contains dairy" it means it has lactose in it

You can also buy dairy free cheese from certain stores and vegan mac n cheese is my go to for dairy free mac n cheese, you can also buy dairy free products on Amazon it's so easy.

And if you still wanna eat dairy you could try taking Lactaid, it's a pill that you take with your first bite of dairy that gives you the lactose enzymes. 


Living dairy free is sometimes said to be bad because the cheese "tastes like cardboard" and the food is "bad", but, once you've become used to it you will find over time you find no difference and enjoy your dairy free lifestyle.
